issues.t: Crankshaft pulley bolt breaks or loosens
issues.sym: A clunk or knocking from the front of the engine, then sudden stalling, heavy steering, a hard brake pedal and a row of warning lights as the belts come off.
issues.why: The bolt that holds the crankshaft pulley and balancer can loosen or snap. The pulley then wobbles or falls off, the accessory belts stop turning, and in bad cases the timing components are damaged too.
issues.next: Pull over safely and do not restart it if the belts are off or you heard a loud clunk. Have it towed and ask the shop to check the timing belt and valves as well as the pulley and bolt.

issues.t: Crankshaft position sensor causes stalling
issues.sym: The engine cuts out at low speed or right after a cold start, may crank but not start, and often restarts after it cools down.
issues.why: The sensor that tells the computer where the crankshaft is can fail intermittently, so the engine loses its spark and fuel timing signal.
issues.next: Have the sensor tested and replaced before relying on the vehicle in traffic, since a stall can happen without warning. Rule out the crank pulley bolt at the same visit.

issues.t: Idle control valve screw can fall into the engine
issues.sym: Rough or unsteady idle, a misfire or check engine light, or a sudden rattling or knocking if a loose part has entered a cylinder.
issues.why: A small screw in the idle control valve could back out and be drawn into the intake, damaging valves and pistons. Kia replaced the valve under a service bulletin and campaign.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer whether the idle control valve campaign was done on your VIN. If the engine starts knocking, stop driving and have it inspected.

issues.t: Fuel line can rub through near the tank (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell around the vehicle or drips under the rear of the body near the tank.
issues.why: Fuel tubes near the tank could touch the floor panel and wear until they leak. Kia recalled affected vehicles and replaced a section of the fuel line.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, do not drive or park it indoors. Check the VIN for the open recall and have the line replaced.

issues.t: ABS module can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay, possibly with the ABS light on, and it can happen with the vehicle parked and turned off.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the anti-lock brake control module and short its circuit board. The recall adds a relay that cuts power to the module when the ignition is off.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and park outside, away from buildings, until it is done. If you see smoke, get out and call for help.

issues.t: Brake light switch failure (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights that do not come on, cruise control that will not cancel with the pedal, a shifter that leaves Park without the brake pressed, push-button start acting up, or the stability control light on.
issues.why: The switch at the top of the brake pedal can work only some of the time. Kia recalled these years and replaced the switch.
issues.next: Have someone watch your brake lights while you press the pedal and check the VIN for the open recall. Get it fixed soon, since drivers behind you rely on those lights.

issues.t: Engine compartment fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke, a burning smell, an oil or fuel smell from under the hood, engine knocking, or warning lights while driving.
issues.why: Kia linked engine fires on these years to internal engine damage and fuel or oil leaks. The recalls add an inspection, engine repair or replacement as needed, and knock-detection software.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and get the inspection and software done. If you see smoke or hear knocking, pull over, shut it off and get out.

issues.t: ABS/HECU control unit fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay, sometimes with the ABS light on, even when the vehicle is parked.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake control unit can short internally, and on 2014-2015 models brake fluid can leak inside it. The recalls add a new fuse and replace leaking units.
issues.next: Run a VIN recall check. If a recall is open, park outdoors away from buildings until the dealer completes the repair.

issues.t: Engine bearing failure and seizure
issues.sym: A knocking that gets louder with engine speed, the check engine or oil light, sudden power loss, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: Machining debris left during manufacturing could restrict oil flow to the connecting rod bearings, which then wear and can seize the engine. Kia recalled many of these engines and added a lifetime short-block warranty tied to a monitoring software update.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear knocking. Check your VIN for open recalls and make sure the knock-detection software update has been installed, since it is required to keep the extended coverage.

issues.t: Fuel pipe leak after an engine replacement (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell from the engine bay, especially on a vehicle that has had its engine replaced.
issues.why: On some engines swapped under the bearing recall, the high-pressure fuel pipe may not have been fitted correctly and can leak near hot parts.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, do not drive it. Check the VIN for this follow-up recall, especially if the engine was ever replaced.

issues.t: Accelerator pedal may stop responding (recall)
issues.sym: Pressing the gas pedal does little or nothing, so the vehicle will not speed up, often with a warning light.
issues.why: A soldering flaw in the accelerator pedal sensor could break the signal to the engine. Kia recalled affected vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. If the pedal stops responding, pull off the road and have it towed.

issues.t: Rear crossmember weld can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, the vehicle pulling or tracking oddly, or uneven rear tire wear.
issues.why: A weld on the rear suspension crossmember may not have been made properly and can break, which upsets rear wheel alignment.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the rear crossmember inspected before highway driving.

issues.t: Shifter may leave Park without the brake (recall)
issues.sym: The shift lever moves out of Park without pressing the brake, or the vehicle rolls after being put in Park.
issues.why: The shift-lock part of the shifter may not lock properly, which can allow a rollaway.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until the recall is done. Check the VIN and book the repair.

issues.t: Multi-function stalk switch contacts wear out
issues.sym: Turn signals, headlights or other stalk functions working only some of the time.
issues.why: Contacts inside the steering column multi-function switch can wear. Kia issued a service campaign and a warranty extension for the switch.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer to check your VIN for the switch campaign and extended coverage, and get it fixed if lights or signals act up.

issues.t: Crankshaft may break and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking or rough running, then a sudden stall while driving.
issues.why: Some crankshafts were not heat treated correctly and can fail. Kia inspects them and replaces the engine assembly where needed.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall right away. If the engine starts knocking, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Tow hitch wiring module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell near the rear of the vehicle, or trailer lights acting up, on vehicles with a Kia trailer hitch harness.
issues.why: Dirt and moisture can collect on the hitch wiring module's circuit board and cause a short, even while parked. Kia replaces the fuse and the module as needed.
issues.next: If you have a Kia tow hitch harness, check the VIN for the recall and park outside until it is repaired.

issues.t: Dual-clutch transmission oil pump can cause loss of power (recall)
issues.sym: Chimes, a transmission warning and a message to stop safely, followed within seconds by the vehicle losing drive.
issues.why: A part on the circuit board of the transmission's electric oil pump can come loose because of faulty soldering. Kia inspects the transmission, replaces it if needed and updates its software.
issues.next: If the warning appears, pull over safely right away. Check the VIN for the recall and have the work done before relying on the vehicle.

issues.t: Front seat belt pretensioner may throw fragments (hybrid recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs beforehand. The danger only shows up when the pretensioners fire in a crash.
issues.why: The front seat belt pretensioners on some Sorento Hybrid and Plug-in Hybrid models could rupture when deployed and send metal pieces into the cabin. Kia fits a protective cap.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and get it done promptly, since it only matters in a crash and gives no warning.

issues.t: Blower motor wiring can melt or catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning or hot plastic smell, smoke from the vents, or the fan stopping, especially on the third fan speed.
issues.why: Wiring to the blower motor resistor was made too thin by a supplier, so the connection can overheat. Kia replaces the harness and the resistor.
issues.next: If you smell burning or see smoke from the vents, turn off the fan, pull over and get out. Avoid fan speed three and check the VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Headlights and taillights can briefly go out (recall)
issues.sym: Low beams and taillights blink off for a moment while driving.
issues.why: A software logic error in the body control unit can momentarily cut the lights. Kia fixes it with a dealer software update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and book the update soon, since it cannot be done over the air. Be extra careful driving at night until then.

issues.t: Fuel line can be damaged in a frontal crash (plug-in hybrid recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving. The risk is a fuel leak after a front-end crash.
issues.why: In some frontal crashes the subframe can shift back and push steering parts into a fuel line. Kia adds a protective cover over the line.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the cover installed. After any front-end crash, have the area checked for fuel leaks.

issues.t: Turbocharger oil supply pipe can crack and leak (recall 22V-202)
issues.sym: A burning oil smell, smoke from under the hood, oil spots under the front of the vehicle or a low oil warning.
issues.why: The pipe that feeds oil to the turbocharger can crack on some vehicles. Leaking oil can land on hot engine and exhaust parts, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell burning oil or see smoke, stop and have it towed. Have a Kia dealer run the VIN for this recall. The pipe is replaced free.

issues.t: Connecting rod bolts may be loose (recall 25V-548)
issues.sym: A knocking noise from the engine that rises with speed, a warning light, then a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: On a limited number of 2025 vehicles the bolts that hold the connecting rods inside the engine may not have been tightened correctly at the factory, and the engine can fail.
issues.next: Have a Kia dealer check the VIN for this recall before driving much further. If the engine starts knocking, pull over and have the vehicle towed. The recall repair is free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag can switch itself off for an adult
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light stays lit with a grown adult sitting in the front passenger seat.
issues.why: The sensor that decides whether the seat holds an adult or a child can read the weight wrongly, so the airbag is disabled when it should be armed.
issues.next: Have the control module reprogrammed under recall 11V-473, and put children in the back in the meantime.

issues.t: Add-on trailer wiring harness can overheat
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell near the rear bumper, melted wiring at the trailer plug, or trailer lights that stop working.
issues.why: An accessory tow harness sold for these years was not watertight, so moisture gets in and the wiring can overheat.
issues.next: Have the harness replaced under recall 11E-041 and do not tow until it is done, because a short back there can start a fire.

issues.t: Water in the camera wiring blanks the backup image
issues.sym: The screen stays black or shows static when you shift into reverse, sometimes only in wet weather.
issues.why: Water tracks into the rear camera connector and corrodes it, so no picture reaches the screen.
issues.next: Have the harness sealed or the camera replaced under recall 23V-639, and turn and look behind you while reversing until then.

issues.t: Rear camera housing clips can break
issues.sym: The reversing picture sits crooked, jiggles, or disappears.
issues.why: The clips holding the camera in the liftgate can snap, letting the camera move out of position.
issues.next: Have the housing replaced under recall 23V-610 and check behind the car yourself while the view is wrong.

issues.t: Power steering wiring may be put together wrongly
issues.sym: The steering suddenly goes heavy, usually with a warning light, and takes much more effort to turn.
issues.why: The wiring to the electric power steering unit may have been assembled incorrectly at the factory, which can cut power to the assist motor.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 24V-287 and have it inspected right away. Losing assist at low speed in a parking lot is hard to handle.

issues.t: Instrument display can go blank from a software fault
issues.sym: The digital gauge cluster goes dark or never lights up, so there is no speed or warning light showing.
issues.why: A software error in the cluster can stop it from starting up properly.
issues.next: Have the software updated under recall 26V-046, over the air or at a dealer. Driving with no speedometer or warning lights is not safe.

issues.t: Wrong spare tire can upset ABS and traction control
issues.sym: After fitting the spare, ABS, traction or stability warning lights come on and braking feels uneven.
issues.why: Some vehicles left the factory with a spare of the wrong size, which makes the wheel speed readings disagree.
issues.next: Have the correct spare fitted under recall 25V-745. If you are on the wrong spare now, drive gently and get it swapped.

issues.t: Cowl crossbar weld can let the steering column move
issues.sym: The steering wheel feels loose or shifts in your hands, or there is a knock from behind the dash when turning.
issues.why: The crossbar behind the dash that supports the steering column may have been poorly welded, so the column can separate from it.
issues.next: Stop driving and check the VIN for recall 18V-656. Losing the steering column's mounting means losing control.
